utterances.text: And with regard to this particular document, was it necessary in your experience or was it not necessary in your experience to identify the sender and the receiver of the transmission? Was it necessary to identify the sender and the receiver of the transmission?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: In order for this document to be in order, it had to be fully filled out and the sender and the receiver had to be indicated clearly, the document had to be signed and stamped. When I sent something, I always had to sign the document, had to indicate what I needed, what quantities, et cetera, and by doing so, I automatically took upon me and the ship where I was the responsibility, I was answerable for these goods, and the warehouse that delivered these goods to me was no longer answerable for the goods, it was no longer in their hands, so at any point in time it could be established where the goods and equipment were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You indicated in your answer that it had to be -- there were a huge number, whatever you requested be it spare parts, fuel, or other equipment or any surplus that I had to return, was it necessary in filling out this document that the area, which I believe is on the one that's up on the screen which is OTP 815, that the nomenclature number and type of supplies be clearly indicated so that all of the parties that are involved in the transaction know precisely what is being requested and what is being sent?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: Precisely so. For example, if spare parts were issued, if I failed to indicate the nomenclature number, and sometimes I didn't know the number but the warehouse person would know the number, and unless that number was clearly indicated, then the goods could not be given to me. The same thing happened when I returned goods. If I was returning something that was no longer in good repair or was something that was decommissioned, the nomenclature number had to be indicated so that the records would be clear and accurate about what was issued, what was returned, what was used up, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. For purposes of clarity and to perfect the record with regard to this particular document, which is 65 ter OTP 815, could you tell us what the form number is of this document, please? Is there a form number on the document? I see at the top of the document a form -- it says "Form MP-20." I don't know whether that's the form number of this document.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: Which document should I be looking at, 815 or 816?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: 815. I believe it's in the upper right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: It says 21/7-2-9.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Up above that it says "O-b-r --" I honestly can't read it myself, I don't know what the word is. It's up at the very top in the right-hand corner. It says Obr and then MP-20.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the upper right corner it says form MP-20. This is the number of the form. Each form had a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And this is the form number for delivery sheets of -- the form number that was used for delivery sheets with regard to such items as ammunition and other military assets that would be delivered; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm now going to move to the next tab in your binder, but before you comment on it, that would be 65 ter OTP 816. Before you comment on it, since this document is similar to the document that we were just discussing except it's entitled a receipt sheet as opposed to a delivery sheet, so that we neither offend the Chamber nor upset the Prosecution, wait until the Prosecution has had a moment to review the document to see whether or not they believe that it will draw an objection or not. So if you would just wait for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But it's still called MP-20.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It is. As is every delivery sheet that we've seen in this trial for some many months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you saying a delivery sheet and a receipt sheet share this number MP-20?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, I am. And I believe that an examination of the evidence that has heretofore been introduced in this case will establish same.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, although the document itself appears to be dated at a time that the General was still chief of the navy and technical administration, however given his general knowledge about delivery sheets such as this, we won't object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would first of all like you to take a look at box number 4, and in box number 4 it has the name of the sender. Could you please read that as it is written in Latinised script? Just read what it says, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I note just for the record, Your Honours, with regard to the English receipt sheet the English translation suffers from something that we went through with a previous witness, I believe it was with General Kodzopeljic, with regard to the fact that on occasion there was a discrepancy between the B/C/S and the English in terms of either the inclusion of information or the exclusion of information, and here, if we look at the English version, we will note that the name and place of sender has been left blank. I'm pointing it out for the record. Also, if I'm not mistaken, if we could go down to the very bottom of the English page, please. As I understand it, this is a translation that was created by the Office of the Prosecutor and is not an official translation. I mention that because at the bottom it says "OTP/DVU." Just for purposes of clarity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't see the OTP/DVU.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you look at the very bottom of the page, left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The name and place of the recipient, if you could read that for us in Serbian, please. That would be at box 14.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: Number 14?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: It says "Command of the Drina Corps."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And looking at the types of materiel that are involved here, as I understand it, the materiel that is involved, if we could go down to the -- stay on the same page in the B/C/S and move to the next page in English, please, so that the Chamber has an opportunity to view what materiel supplies are being sent by the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm looking at this list and I'm doing this generically. It would be fair to say that this list is comprised of mortars, rocket-launchers, mines, and bullets, bullets for a number of different types -- bullets of different types; 7.62, 7.9, 1.22; various types of bullets. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, continuing with -- that's sufficient. That's sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would move for its admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You indicated that you are not objecting?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: No, I'm not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D449. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please switch off his microphone when not using it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do apologise. Too many pieces paper in front of me at the moment but I'll be more mindful of that. If we could now look at 65 ter OTP 818, which is going to be tab number 27 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And before you make any comments with regard to this document, I'm going to take the same position that I took with the last document. I don't know whether or not, after review, this will draw an objection or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would just again note, in relation to the date, this far predates this witness's direct knowledge of it, however I have no objections to him talking about these forms generally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to this document, I'd like to go through the same exercise that we went through in the last document. Could you please tell us, looking at the Serbian version of this, who the sender is and who -- first of all in box number 4, and who the receiver is in box number 14.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: The sender is the minister of defence of the Republic of Serbia, and the receiver is the command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the types of materiel that are being discussed in this particular document, could you tell us what types of materiel they are, please? Just generally, would it be fair to say we are once again talking about bullets, mortars and grenades?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so. That's what is written on this sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would move this document 's admission, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D450. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: 65 ter OTP 820, which will be 28 in your binder. And I would go through the same exercise I've gone through before, so that we don't engage in unnecessary argument. I don't know what the Prosecution's position is with regard to this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, until the witness is allowed opportunity to show that he does have some relation or some knowledge about this document, we believe that it would be premature to provide any objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: First of all, could you tell us whether or not you can -- it may be a bit difficult. Can you read the very top of the document. In English I have the statement: "Receipt for the above-mentioned military property received for temporary use from Republic of Serbia Defence Ministry." I don't know if that reads the same in your copy in B/C/S at the very top of the document. If you could just say yes or no, if it does, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: No, it says here: "Receipt for the above-mentioned military property received for temporary use from the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the items that are listed there, once again, are those items -- would it be fair to characterise those six items as grenades, mines, and ammunition for --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: Precisely so. This comes from the ammunition arsenal which was used by the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned the Territorial Defence, which is something that I think we'll briefly touch upon after the break because I'm looking at the clock and I think His Honour is too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Guy-Smith. We'll take a break and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Right before the break you mentioned the Territorial Defence. Could you briefly describe to the Chamber what the Territorial Defence was.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: In keeping with the constitution of the former state of the SFRY, and in keeping with the strategy of defence, each republic had a Territorial Defence, which was an army parallel to the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to this parallel army, as you've discussed it, called the Territorial Defence, did this army have its own military equipment, its own supplies, or were those supplies part of the former JNA?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: It was not by chance that I mentioned the word "parallel" because at the beginning, at the outset, we had armed forces which had two components; the Territorial Defence and the Yugoslav People's Army. However, in practice and subsequent events showed that those two components of the armed forces were broken up and went each its own separate way. The Territorial Defence was equipped and financed by the republics. Each republic allocated, in keeping with the law, a certain amount of money, it established its own units, and in practical terms, those units were subordinated to the republican leaderships.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And just a minor point of clarification. You indicated the Territorial Defence was equipped and financed by the republics. With regard to the Territorial Defence being equipped by the republics, what kind of equipment did the republics supply to the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: The republics financed the needs of the Territorial Defence. It was not that each republic bought what they wanted. There was a system in place for the procurement of all republican territorial defences and there was a system co-ordinated with the then Secretariat For National Defence and the equipment was not of an offensive nature, of the same nature as the JNA had. It was primarily for the mass defence of the territory and the protection of the population, production facilities, and the like. That was the main purpose of the Territorial Defence equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm now returning to the document we've been discussing, OTP 65 ter 820. With regard to this particular document, can you tell us what involvement, if any, the VJ had with regard to the types of military property that are indicated here?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: I did not understand your question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Surely. Was -- to your knowledge, if you are looking at this document, can you tell us whether or not this document involved the VJ in any fashion?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: This document does not imply the participation of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd move its admission.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we find ourselves in the same position we were this morning; there's not been a link made between this witness and this document. We are no longer dealing with the MP-20 delivery slips and all the witness has been asked to do is confirm the contents of the document itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm not going to go through the long argument that we went through before. I believe that a sufficient basis has been established and, interestingly, the Prosecution previously did not object to one of the self-same documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I -- with respect to 815, as I understood it, the ruling was that the objection was upheld, Judge Picard dissenting, and I've now been told that 815 is D448. This is what confuses us. I still don't understand, because it looks like the decision is going to go along the same lines. Mr. Registrar, you gave us to understand that 815 was D448 and at the time when the ruling came out I noted that the objection was upheld, Judge Picard dissenting. And if the objection was upheld, it would then mean that it was not admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be corrected. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the situation we are in now, which is a slightly different document, this is an MP-32 document, not an MP-20 document, we had a discussion about a previous document which was 65 ter TP 810 which became D447, for which the Prosecution did not object. This is the self-same type of document. And it was on that basis that I -- it was on that basis that I proceeded with this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Having not had an objection levied previously, otherwise I would have handled this document in an entirely different fashion. But if we want to have disparate views with regard to the self-same document in terms of evidence, so be it. The record will be -- will ultimately end up being a dog's breakfast in that regard for your purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is a dog's breakfast because at that time when you tendered 810, the Prosecution didn't object and if now they are objecting to the admission of this one and they have a valid objection, it should be upheld because this is where the objection first comes. But if it is not upheld, it must be upheld -- it must be dismissed on the basis that the document is admissible, not because a previous one was admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I appreciate that. As I said to you before, rather than go through the entirety of the argument I posited before, in order to save time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You repeat it by reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm repeating it by reference and I'm relying upon the fact that when this document -- when the self-same document -- excuse me, when a similar document essentially identical in nature was proffered for admission, there was no objection. So I add that on to -- I add that on to the argument that was made before, because clearly what is happening is we are getting disparate positions taken. But as I said before, you know, the dilemma will be ultimately at the end in the terms of analysis that we all have to go through and the kinds of evidence we rely upon and whatever errors may or may not exist as a result of the disparate views that have been taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then in that event, the objection would then be upheld, Judge Picard still dissenting.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. If we could now turn to --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just for the record, Exhibit D448 is hereby withdrawn from the court record and will be marked not admitted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter OTP document again 822, which will be tab 29 in your binder, sir. Now, with regard to -- the document isn't up on the screen yet. With regard to this document, I trust I'm understanding Ms. Carter's position correctly and this is a document that she would not be objecting to, this being a delivery sheet, but before I proceed any further, I wish to make sure and have some confidence in that position. I'm only doing this to save time with regard to argument.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, as to this document, similarly to the other MP-20 forms, we acknowledge that the witness has some general competence to testify in regards to them. I would just note yet again that the date of this is well before the witness takes the position in which he had contact with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Carter. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the document that's presently before you, could you tell us, please, looking at item number 4, the name of the sender?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: The sender is the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The receiver, looking at box number 14?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: The receiver is the command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the types of military product that are being transferred here are generally bullets, mortars, projectiles for rocket-launchers, and grenades; is that fair?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct. And this is materiel from the supplies of the Territorial Defence of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to what you just said, what involvement, if any, did the VJ have with regard to this particular transaction?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Carter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object to speculation on this point. This witness wouldn't have been in a position -- in August of 1993 he was still with the navy technical institute. To have him actually speak to this specific transaction and what the VJ's involvement was would exceed his competency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let me rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the matters concerning the Ministry of Defence for the Republic of Serbia, are you familiar with the methodology that existed as between requests for particular military resources and the methodology that was used by the Ministry of Defence for Serbia in terms of accommodating those requests?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: A slight digression before that, if I may. As a desk officer in the navy and technical administration, before I became chief, I was in charge of diving, sabotage, and other types of equipment. I was directly engaged and I helped the Territorial Defence of the Republic of Serbia with regard to the procurement of the equipment. I'm familiar with the depot where that materiel was stored. So I'm very familiar with that area. On the other note, the Army of Yugoslavia did not have anything to do with this particular matter. The only thing that may be similar or the same is the calibre of the rounds that were procured.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I move this document's admission.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: No objection to the admission, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D451. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before this document is removed from the screen, I have a question for the witness. Under box 4 it states that this equipment comes from the Ministry of Defence from the the Republic of Serbia. A moment ago you said that the Republic of Serbia should in fact be Republika Srpska. You stated that in reference to one of the other documents. Is this also the case? Are we talking here about Serbia or the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know where the confusion comes from. It is clear that the Republic of Serbia was part of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia whereas Republika Srpska is in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I really don't want to create any confusion. The two are not in any direct connection. They are not administratively connected at all. They are two completely different entities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I realise that, that's why I asked the question. But at one point in time the document stated RS, you said it could only be Republika Srpska, whereas the translation said Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how things are translated. I'm reading B/C/S documents and it's spelled out, the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia. I'm not assuming or supposing things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, your answer is perfect. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, as at the 23rd of August, 1993, did the state of Serbia exist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The state existed and together with Montenegro it constituted the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. The former two were the components of one and the same state and the Supreme Defence Council was composed of the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, the president of Montenegro, and the president of Serbia. Three members, three people were members of the Supreme Defence Council of the former state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You see, now, let me tell you where the confusion comes. The confusion comes where you told us earlier that Republic of Serbia could only mean Republika Srpska because the state of Serbia did not exist, it was the FRY at the time. That's what you told us earlier, sir. Now you are saying the state of Serbia at this date existed with Montenegro and Serbia together called the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, at that time it was not called Serbia, it was called Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, so we are -- at least I understood you to mean that where we see Republic of Serbia before the existence of Serbia it refers to the Republika Srpska, but now I think you are taking a different position in answering Judge Picard.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think perhaps there's a bit of confusion. I don't think he is taking a different position. Let me see if I can clarify the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please clarify the record because a number of documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Understood, understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but a number of exhibits have come in since that last explanation where the Republic of Serbia in the English is written and we need all that to be cleared.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let me see what I can do for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was comprised of what constituent parts?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was comprised of the Republic of Serbia and the Republic of Montenegro. The then president of Serbia was Slobodan Milosevic and the president of Montenegro at the time was Momir Bulatovic, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the issue presented upon the formation of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, did the Republic of Serbia -- from what you've said, did the Republic of Serbia exist or did it not exist?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: The Republic of Serbia never stopped existing. It existed in the SFRY and it continued existing thereafter. All the republics existed from the year 1945.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the existence of the Republika Srpska, can you tell us when the Republika Srpska first came into existence?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: If my memory serves me well, and I must say that I'm not always good with dates, I believe that they proclaimed its existence on the 9th of January, 1992, or perhaps 1993. No, it was in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I noted that Judge Picard was shaking her head so I'm gathering that I'm not getting to a point of clarification for her. With that in mind, I'm going to continue to try to get to a point of clarification for her because I have no desire to waste the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you do that, and I think this is the reason she is shaking her head, taking into account the answer to the previous question where the witness says the Republic of Serbia always existed, take note of that answer and then look at page 28, line 21 to 24 where he then -- where he said --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I am aware of that, Your Honour, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I am aware of that, Your Honour. I'm going to get us to that point. It seemed to me essentially what we had to do first was engage in some kind of a basic history understanding as to what existed and what did not exist at what period of time, with that in mind, because I think that is of some assistance because I think there are matters actually which in fact the Court can take judicial notice of and something that we've discussed repeatedly here. But I wanted to get some clarification with regard to that first and then address the specific language that's contained there that is causing the Chamber concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It looks like the witness wants to say something, Mr. Guy-Smith. I don't know whether you want to let him say it or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, because I want to make sure I'm on track. Could you do me a favour, please, and please put D446 back on the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, your response to this document I think is what has generated the present confusion that we are involved in, so I'd like to go back and take a look at this document. What is the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: The date is 16 March 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Reading the B/C/S version of the document, could you please read the second line, starting with the word "Da." Just read that line out loud, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: "The Ministry of Defence of the Republika Srpska ensure consent for the overhaul in the Hadzici RZ or in the Cacak TRZ of the following pieces of equipment."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Stop right there. Now, when we were talking about this document before, you were asked the following question, and I'm going to truncate my question starting at line 16 on page 27. I said: "In the text of this document --" then I listed it out, and then I asked the following question: "With respect -- with regard that your Ministry of Defence or some other Ministry of Defence, if you know." And your answer is as follows, and here is where the confusion is right now: "I know that this is the Ministry of Defence of the Republika Srpska." And then you go on and say some things, then at line -- at line -- sorry, at line 1 --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Then you go on and you say at line 21, and in response to a question of Judge Moloto's, sir: "Just before we admit it, let's just get the record clear. The English translation here reads: 'Through the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia.' You are saying Republika Srpska. Is that what stands on the B/C/S version, or in other words, is the English translation incorrect?" Please. Now, your response to the Judge was: "Mr. President, the translation is incorrect because the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia did not exist at this point in time. Only the Federal Ministry of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia existed at this period in time." So you have told us that there was the Republic of Serbia, and the question that I think logically follows from the confusion that has been created is as follows: Did the Republic of Serbia continue or cease to continue to have a Ministry of Defence after the formation of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: The Republic of Serbia, after the break-up of the SFRY, had a Ministry of Defence, and the first minister of defence was Admiral Jokic. I know the man. Later on he was an accused here in The Hague and he was convicted. When Serbia and Montenegro merged into the FRY, the function of the minister of defence were quenched in these two republics and the duties were transferred on to the federal minister of defence, hence only the Federal Ministry of Defence existed and although the republics existed, they did not have their respective Ministry of Defence. They transferred their defence ministry and their Ministry of Foreign Affairs on to the federal state.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think that takes care of one part of what may be the confusion. I think therein lies another question, and I'm picking this -- I have a question but I think you may have a different question, so I will -- I'm happy to see whether or not your question is going to take care of my question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. If you want me to ask, my question was going to be, when you answered here to say that the Ministry of Defence of Serbia is the ministry that supplied these goods, were you referring to the area that is today called Serbia which at the time within the FRY was a republic of the FRY?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you then saying that the VRS Main Staff is being requested here to supply these goods through the ministry of Serbia in Serbia and not the ministry of Serbia in Republika Srpska? Because you have just told us that when you said the Ministry of Defence of Serbia, you meant the ministry of the Republic of Serbia which was the republic within the FRY. It's confusing even more.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I hope it is confusing even less, but I think that it is reasonable and logical to, and I am not saying assume but to find, that when you have the Latinised letters MORS, that you are referring to or one is referring to the Ministry of Defence for the Republika Srpska. I think that is a particular kind of nomenclature that we have seen throughout these proceedings. With that in mind and my assumption would be -- now I'm making an assumption by reading the English translation -- that the English translation is incorrect, which is independent of the issue -- which is independent of the issue that he has raised. I believe that the English translation should properly read, "secure an approval through the Ministry of Defence of the Republika Srpska for a maintenance in RZ," and continuing with the language therein. That would, to me, be a logical and consistent translation based upon what we have seen for close to two years in terms of the document itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I hear what you say, Mr. Guy-Smith, and unfortunately the situation here is that whereas that's how I understood the witness at page 28, now when he speaks latterly, he is no longer stating the same position. At page 28 he said the Republic of Serbia did not exist at that time. Now he says Republic of Serbia has always existed, has always been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think this is where we may be a bit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And for me, it looks to me like when he says Republic of Serbia has always existed, he is talking of Republic of Serbia as a republic within the SFRY, within the FRY, and today as a state. And yet when he said earlier, at page 28, that the Republic of Serbia did not exist he was referring to Republic of Serbia as a state, as a country.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might, Your Honour. If I might, Your Honour, I think this might be where some of the confusion lies. He said at line 21: "Because the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia." Not the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Naturally, naturally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Ministry of Defence of Republic of Serbia did not exist. But he has just told us that at that time the republics used to have their own financing and procurement, equipment of arms to the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Through which ministry?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, we haven't discovered through which ministry, if any ministry. I think part of -- I think part of the dilemma is as follows, which is that it's part of what we have been attempting to do for you. During the transitional period it is not either reasonable, logical, or in fact accurate to assume that there were hard and fast - I'll put it in those terms - organs, and we've talked about this as a transitional period or transformation period, and I think that you will find, and I don't want to put these words into the witness's mouth, but it's one of the things that we are going to talk about later --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- talk about later, which is really what is the state of affairs? And I think that an attempt to rigidly define some of these things won't work terribly well and it other places it will work. But is that is obviously the nature of a conflict-torn area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. Madam Carter, do you have any contribution to make to this discussion?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. In the context of what you have been speaking about, you covered the contribution I was going to make earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Mr. Guy-Smith, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is there something that you wish to say?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. What do you wish to say, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: Just what we have already said. I don't understand the confusion because everything is evident. I simply said that at that time in 1994 there did not exist the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia. However, the republic itself did exist. You can see it based on the document which is on the screen. This institution here writes to the Main Staff of the VRS. Neither in Serbia nor in Yugoslavia there existed a Main Staff. There was no such institution within Serbia or Yugoslavia, which is to say that this is a document emanating from Republika Srpska. So this institution is writing to its Main Staff, asking them to address their request to the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska because the repair facility, the service facility in Hadzici, is located in Republika Srpska. So this was their internal institution, internal relations, it was a completely internal transaction within Republika Srpska. And I don't see what is confusing here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I hear that answer. I would like the witness, if he could, to give us an answer similar to that with respect to the document that raised Judge Picard's issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. And which document is that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought it was D451. The last document that was on the monitor --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. The last document that was on the monitor when Judge Picard asked --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Perfect.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you could go to tab 29 in your binder. Tab 29. You may well still be there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If we could have it on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could have it up on the screen, that would be -- it's now D451.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's right. The name of the sender.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This document, unlike the document that we were looking at before, does not have the Latinised letters of MORS. It has something written I think both -- letters and something written out. So looking at the name of the sender, could you tell us what it says in box number 4?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: Under 4 it says an acronym, Ministry of Defence of the Republic, that is an an acronym, and then Serbia is spelled out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say Serbia is spelled out, just for purposes of the record, could you tell us what the letters are. Unlike before where we had an acronym, now we have a name, a full name. Could you tell us what the letters are in fact?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: S-r-b-i-j-a.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: To your knowledge and your experience in living in the region, did RS ever stand for Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: Acronym RS was used for Republika Srpska, not for the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My question to you was going to be which geographical unit within the former SFRY does this Serbia here refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This refers to the entire area except for Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The entire area of the former SFRY? My question was to which geographical unit within the former SFRY does this Serbia here refer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This pertains to a geographical unit within the the SFRY. If we exclude the Republic of Slovenia, Republic of Croatia, Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Republic of Macedonia and the Republic of Montenegro, what remains is the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess it excluded Croatia as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that under number 2. In that case, the interpreter didn't interpret it. I mentioned it after Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm with you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I started from the west.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think I can be of some further assistance to all of you -- I think I can be some further assistance to all of you with asking of two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm quite happy that the first Serbia was RS Republika Srpska, this one refers to Serbia as we mean Serbia today. But I just don't know where the cutoff comes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think that's where I'm probably going to and I want to make sure -- or to the extent that I can, I want to make Judge Picard happy too here with regard to this particular issue for purposes of clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you could take a look at the document, please, could you tell us the date of this document, General? Looking up in the upper right-hand corner, do you see the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the date is the 23rd of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you had mentioned to us in your testimony that there came a time when the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia transferred its competency to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and ceased to exist. Now, as you sit here today, can you tell us whether or not it would be accurate that the Ministry of Defence for the Republic of Serbia existed until the end of 1993 or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia officially came into existence on the 27th of April, 1994, when the constitution was adopted in the federal parliament. However, prior to that time, as the political elite had decided to establish such a state while the constitution was being written, the ministries of defence in the republics which formed the Federation slowly ceased to exist, because it couldn't be done overnight, and then they completely ceased to exist once the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was created. So the process of the ministries and the republics dying out was a process. The date of 27th of April was celebrated as the statehood day, the day when the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was founded. The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia no longer exists today.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand that. And looking at line 24, you have the date as the 27th of April, 1994. Is that accurate, 1994?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: I think that this is when the FRY was created and when the constitution was passed and other laws and regulations. I'm not a hundred per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We've heard the date previously of 1992, so that's the reason I'm asking the question.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: They started functioning to some extent but they did not manage to pass the constitution and other laws and regulations, so for awhile there was a transition period. I may not be the best person to ask for the date, but I remember that we had numerous problems in our work because the set of laws and regulations that we needed in order to work was not yet in place at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to try to move to an area where hopefully we will not fall into the muddle of confusion but can deal with things that are relatively simple.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And in that regard if we could please have up on the screen P1201, which would be tab 26 in your binder, sir -- I'm sorry, tab 16 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to start at the very top of this document, and at the very top of this document it indicates in English on the left-hand side "army post office number 1089-30." As I read this document, this document is referring to an army post office. Am I correct in my assumption there?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This document was registered with the military post 1089-30.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And what military post is that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: This is the military post which was the procurement administration within the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: I know that for a number of reasons, the main one being that I used to work in the Ministry of Defence and this administration was a parallel administration to the one where I worked. I worked with them every day. While I worked at the General Staff each request for procurement had this military post indicated on it. I know this because I signed all of those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you tell us the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: The 29th of March, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And what is the subject matter of this document? I'm looking once again just at the very top where in English it says "Delivery of Contract".

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: This is an accompanying letter enclosed with the document it was sent with. Military post 1089-30, which is the procurement administration, sent a contract on a loan. And this was the accompanying document. This document also indicates to which military posts it was delivered.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And who are the the contracting parties with regard to the loan of 42.72 tonnes of TNT?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: The contracting parties were research, development, and manufacturing administration on the one side and the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the research, development, and manufacturing administration on the one side is part of what organ? Is that part of the VJ, part of the Ministry of Defence, part of the Ministry of the Interior? Who does the research, development, and manufacturing administration belong to?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: Research, development, and manufacturing administration was part of the military economic sector of the Federal Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And what involvement, if any, if you know, did the research, development, and manufacturing administration of the military economic sector of the Federal Ministry of Defence have with the VJ in terms of negotiating contracts?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: Could you be more specific, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Surely. Did the VJ have any involvement in this contract?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: No. No, except for the administration for research, development, and manufacturing and the administration for procurement. Both of them are part or were part of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Looking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure I understand what the answer says when it says, "No. No, except for ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's what my concern is right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I asked you the following question, which is : "Did the VJ have any involvement in this contract?" And you said: "No. No, except for the administration for research, development, and manufacturing and the administration for procurement. Both of them are part or were part of the Ministry of Defence." So let me ask you the question again, which is, did the VJ have any involvement in this contract?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: No, the VJ did not participate in this contract. They did not conclude the contract with the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska. However, later on it appears as a participant in the stage of the delivery of the materiel to the place where it would be stored.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand. That's not my question at the moment. Looking again at page -- at the very first page, it says at the very bottom of the very first page, on the right-hand side: "PO." Then there are two words, and underneath that there's another word and then there's a signature. Could you tell us what it says where it says "PO" -- the acronym "PO" and the two words that follow there?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: This means that the document was signed under the authority of the chief of that particular administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say "under the authority," PO, the next word is "Ovlascenju." Sorry, I probably made a mess of the way its pronounced in Serbian. What is that word after PO? Ovla? Looking at the document.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: The main role of the chief of administration or any other body is to sign documents. In this particular case this means that this person was authorised --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, I'm asking you a very straight question right now, a very particular question here, which is what does that say? Specifically PO and then there are two words that follow. What does that say? Just read it in Serbian, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: Under the authority of the chief Lieutenant-Colonel Stanisa Bakic, which means that the chief of that administration authorised that person to forward this document and that he was authorised to sign it and to stamp it. And that's it. This person who signed the document was not the decision-maker in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The English translation reads "PO of Chief of Staff." Would that be an accurate translation?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before this page disappears, can I just clear one little point. You answered earlier when you were asked about the VJ involvement, you said: "No, the VJ did not participate. However, later on it appears as a participant in the stage of the delivery of the materiel to the place where it would be stored." Can you show us where that appears? Where it appears that the VJ is a participant, from the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the document was drafted or when the contract was concluded and when the decision was taken on the loan, the VJ did not participate because it wasn't its materiel and they were not the decision-maker, but when the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you. I'm asking you not about the conclusion of the contract. I am asking you about the delivery. You say it appears that the VJ was involved in the delivery of the materiel. I just want you to tell us from this document where we can see that involvement of the VJ in the delivery.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you look at the left bottom corner, there are the addressees, the first one is military post 8634-3 Belgrade, and that's the sector for military economic activity and the chief of sector is hereby allowed to follow the progress of the events. And then the army appears, military post office 9808, that's the 608th Logistics Base. And there's also military post office 9808-6 which is the Lunjevica depo near Gornji Milanovac. That is the base depot, and they were supposed to act on the contract and deliver goods from the federal commodity reserves. Not from the military commodity reserves but from the federal commodity reserves, that the base was in charge of safeguarding explosives pursuant to the same regulations which were binding upon the military. And this was due to the fact that the materiel in question was hazardous, that's why the military looked after it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Earlier in your testimony, if I'm not mistaken, you indicated that as the chief of research and development you were authorised to dispose of or otherwise alienate raw materials. I just want to make sure I'm correct in that regard.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: You are absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, with regard to the raw material that is being discussed in this contract, in one of your recent answers you indicated who the owner was of this material or where this material came from. And who is the -- if looking at Article 2 of this particular contract, does that indicate the kind -- who is the owner of the raw materials, and by that I mean the language here which says federal material reserve?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And who is the owner of this raw material?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: The owner of this raw material is the federal government.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, as I understand this document, this document is a contract in which a price was set for the value of this material which is found above Article 2 in which it says, at least in English, total value of the contracted goods, subject of this loan, according to this contract, calculated by creditor at the price of 4,85 n dinars per kilogram, is, and there is the amount of 207.192 n dinars. Now, for purposes of our understanding, who is the creditor that calculated the price of these raw materials?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: The price of the material was calculated by the procurement administration which was otherwise tasked with determining all the prices. The pricing of the goods purchased, the goods sold, as well as the price of a working hour in the service.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the procurement administration, are you referring to the Ministry of Defence or the procurement administration that we have been discussing throughout the day?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, precisely so, I'm talking about the procurement administration of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There are a series of other parts of this contract, but I'd like to just get to Article 7 in the contract here, which deals with dispute resolution. In the event of a dispute with regard to this particular transaction, where is the jurisdiction to be found under Article 7?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC
utterances.text: According to this contract, it will be the military arbitration with the Federal Ministry of Defence that will be in charge. That was an organ, a body that was in existence and a body that was in charge of such matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would be moving on to another subject, so it may be an appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Kadijevic, unfortunately we are not done with you. You'll have to come back tomorrow. Just to warn you that while you are on recess between now and tomorrow, you are not supposed to discuss this case with anybody and least of all the Defence until such time as you are released from further testifying. The case is going to stand adjourned to tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning in the same courtroom here. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 7th day of September, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.42 p.m.
